items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: pay the Basie orchestra what they get

ctx.x: Oh sure. Oh sure. And you know even though I’m not terribly organized, I have spreadsheet programs where I put all the — some of it you have to guess at — but sure, when you raise money that’s part of what you raise money for. You have the whole overhead thing. You need an accountant. You need an attorney to advise you. You need someone to look over the releases and see if they’re okay, and then the music clearances, which — as you and I both know very well — we did this documentary on Joe Williams and there was…

good, because I just got out of the way and let Joe be himself. But it will never be seen on television unless we raise another fifty grand or so to clear all the music licenses and pay the Basie orchestra what they get — scale for television, which is a different thing from playing in a concert hall. And all this extra money has to be raised. So yeah.
Yeah, Jean Bach, “A Great Day in Harlem.”
